extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for Taylor & Francis journals (all disciplines)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers assessing manuscripts submitted to Taylor & Francis journals, including ethical duties, core assessment factors, review-quality standards, and best practices. Applicable across manuscript types (research articles, reviews, case studies, humanities, STEM, opinion pieces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the originality of the manuscript's subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide advice on the originality, presentation, and relevance of the manuscript's subject matter to the readership of the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the clarity, organization, and overall presentation of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should provide advice on the presentation of the manuscript as part of assessing its suitability for the journal's readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to readership
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge whether the manuscript's topic is relevant to the journal's audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how the subject matter fits the readership of the journal when advising on the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and validity of methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the study's methods are appropriate, accurate, and valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should provide advice on the accuracy and validity of the methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions appropriately supported
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the manuscript's conclusions are supported by the data and analysis presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the conclusions are appropriately supported by the results and argumentation in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unbiased consideration / non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: Give unbiased consideration and judge each manuscript on its merits regardless of author characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review without regard to race, religion, nationality, gender, seniority, or institutional affiliation of the author(s). This is an ethical requirement to be met before agreeing to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare any conflicts of interest before agreeing to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must declare any relationship with the author(s) or other circumstances that may bias their review prior to accepting the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the peer review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep manuscript content and correspondence confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share information or correspondence about a manuscript with anyone outside of the peer review process without the explicit permission of the editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: No use of AI tools to generate review reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use artificial intelligence tools (including LLMs like ChatGPT) to generate manuscript review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit prohibition: reviewers must not use AI tools to generate manuscript review reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use manuscript-type-specific checklists
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply the publisher's specialized checklists tailored to the manuscript type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taylor & Francis offers specialized checklists for different manuscript types: STEM research articles, arts and humanities research articles, review articles, case studies, and position/opinion pieces. Use the appropriate checklist for the submission type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide actionable suggestions that help authors improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be constructive — providing actionable suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover all major aspects of the paper in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be comprehensive — covering all major aspects of the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidenced claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Base reviewer claims on specific reasoning and evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be evidenced — claims backed by specific reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate substance / sufficient detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the review has an appropriate level of detail; not too brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews should be appropriately substantial — not too brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the article fully before judging
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the entire manuscript before forming judgments or recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: read the article fully before forming judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note strengths and weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and report both positive aspects and deficiencies of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: note both strengths and weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific page/line references
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite specific locations in the manuscript when pointing out issues or examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific page/line references when possible to support comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish major from minor concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly separate critical, substantive problems from minor issues or stylistic matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: distinguish major from minor concerns so editors and authors understand priorities for revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on manuscript content, not authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique the work itself rather than the authors or their attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the manuscript's content rather than authors when composing the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect journal scope and mission
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess suitability of the manuscript with regard to the journal's stated scope and mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best practice: respect the journal's scope and mission when evaluating whether a manuscript is appropriate.
